content.title: About
content.content: Peanut butter is a paste made from ground peanuts, enriched with a modest amount of sugar for a gentle sweetness. It retains the characteristic nutty flavor while containing less sugar than traditional versions, making it a better choice for those monitoring sugar intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter is a staple in Asian cuisine, especially in sauces and marinades.
Reducing sugar lets the natural peanut aroma shine through more clearly.
Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts, giving them a distinct nutrient profile.
In the United States, lower‑sugar peanut butter is often marketed as “light” or “reduced sugar.”
Peanut butter can be smooth or crunchy, depending on consumer preference.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Peanut butter provides monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Approximately 25 % of peanut butter’s weight is protein, beneficial for muscle repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals aid normal nerve function and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Lower sugar content
items.content: Reduced sugar helps maintain steadier blood glucose levels.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; reactions can be severe and require medical attention.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite lower sugar, the spread remains calorie‑dense, so portion control is important.

items.title: Aflatoxin presence
items.content: Poor‑quality peanuts may contain aflatoxins—toxins that necessitate sourcing from reputable producers.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Some brands add salt or preservatives; check the label if you need to limit sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread peanut butter on toast, stir into smoothies, use in sauces, bake with it, or add to energy bars. For a softer texture, gently warm the spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard if it develops a rancid odor.
